text:
maria: noticing repeated nvme write stalls and a spike in tinywrites on us-east4-ephemeral around 03:12 UTC. GPU attach started failing intermittently and a few batch jobs fell back.

ash: which pool? any iostat snippet?

maria: pool ep-east4-b. sample: ```iostat -x 1 2
Device: r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await %util
nvme0n1 1.0 420.0 8.0 11000.0 52.0 6.8 14.2 99.7
```

ravi: that avgqu and util are saturated. timeline?

maria: scrub controller shows many concurrent verify jobs; scheduler returned 429s then multi-host scrub starts overlapped with peak attach window. ops-bot: "scheduler rate-limit triggered cohort ep-east4-b"

ash: quick options: 1) apply temporary scrub backoff 2) cordon worst hosts 3) bump attach timeout to reduce immediate fallback. I vote 1+3.

ravi: agree. also reduce scrub concurrency and add a per-pool coalesce window so we don't hit multiple hosts simultaneously.

maria: applying: `scheduler set-backoff --pool ep-east4-b --duration 900s` and `autoscaler attach_timeout=60s -> 120s` rolled to canary.

ops-bot: "action: set-backoff accepted by scheduler; canary rollout started"

ash: watching graphs: nvme avgqu dropped to ~2 within 4m, attach success recovered. we'll keep backoff 15m, then reintroduce scrubs with coalesce guard.

maria: filing follow-ups: firmware parity check, scrub-priority review, and add hysteresis to scheduler. logging cost bump from fallbacks in incident-costs. will post if it recurs. :thumbsup:
